biography.plain_text: David Davidovich is a Russian businessman whose career spans oil trading, industrial investment and food production. After senior commercial roles in energy and asset management, he established PRODO as a consolidated agricultural and meat-processing group. He became its controlling shareholder as the business grew into one of Russia's largest producers of meat and poultry.

long_biography.plain_text:
PRODO brought processing plants, poultry farms, pig complexes and animal-feed production into a single industrial group. David Davidovich formed the holding in 2004 after working in oil trading and corporate asset management. The structure joined agricultural inputs with branded food manufacturing, giving the business control over much of its supply chain.

Within several years, the group reported substantial positions in Russian meat products, poultry and pork. Its portfolio included regional brands and a network of farms and factories spread across several federal districts. Davidovich held a controlling interest during the company's expansion, while professional managers directed its operations. He later ceased to be a shareholder. Corporate-registry reporting showed that another owner controlled the entire group by December 2024.
